checks.location: Higher-body-order density trick and Algorithm1 looped tensor contraction; equivariant coupling rationale
checks.claim: Higher-body-order density trick and Algorithm1 looped tensor contraction; equivariant coupling rationale
checks.explanation: No error found in the selected density-factorization and contraction argument. Its inclusion of repeated indices is essential and explicitly stated.
checks.demonstration: For one-particle features A_a=sum_j phi_a(j), distributivity gives product_{s=1}^nu A_{a_s}=sum_{j1,...,jnu} product_s phi_{a_s}(j_s), including repetitions. Therefore generalized CG contraction of the product realizes the ordered-neighbor many-body expansion without enumerating neighbor tuples. Composition of CG intertwiners preserves the specified representation; summation over neighbors preserves permutation symmetry. Algorithm1 is multivariate Horner evaluation: starting with C_nu contracted once with A, successively add C_k and contract again; induction yields sum_{k=1}^nu C_k:A^tensor(k). An independent nu4 random-tensor check and explicit four-neighbor nu3 expansion agree to floating-point precision. Computation is linear in neighbor count at fixed tensor sizes; it is not uniformly independent of feature width or correlation order.
checks.scope: No full audit of the infinite-feature universality assertion cited to ACE, finite-width injectivity, learning-curve slopes, or empirical force-field accuracy. First-layer body order is with respect to atomic states; later states already depend on multiple positions. The printed Algorithm1 suppresses optional feature mixing, so the algebra is checked on the features actually entering the tensor products.
checks.claimContext: Products of summed one-particle features expand into the ordered-neighbor many-body sums, including repeated neighbors, and the stated equivariant contractions can be computed without enumerating all tuples.
